scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The 'About This Report' section opens in first-person plural ('We audited', 'We fetch', 'We then review') but the 'Executive Summary' and all subsequent Findings priority blocks also use first-person plural consistently — however, the 'Recommended Actions' list in 'Next Steps' switches to impersonal imperative/third-person constructions ('address the 29 WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility issues', 'Structured Data improvements') while every other action-oriented section in the report uses first-person plural voice.
findings.context: 1. **Address Priority 1 findings**: address the 29 WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility issues identified (regulatory exposure)

findings.message: The 'Structured Data Inventory' section asserts 'a wider audit identifies the same gaps across the rest of the estate' — this projects a sample finding (0/100 structured data on 7 pages) as a confirmed fact about the full site without qualification.
findings.context: a wider audit identifies the same gaps across the rest of the estate.

findings.message: The 'Marker Reachability' section states 'a wider audit confirms whether the same pattern holds across the rest of the estate', which is correctly hedged, but the preceding sentence asserts 'All detected markers are present in the served HTML on the pages we audited' and then adds 'Server-side and browser-based agents see the same signals on the sampled pages' — this is fine — however the sentence 'a wider audit confirms whether the same pattern holds' is inconsistent with the unhedged assertion two sentences earlier that treats the sampled finding as a site-wide statement.
findings.context: All detected markers are present in the served HTML on the pages we audited. Server-side and browser-based agents see the same signals on the sampled pages

findings.message: Priority 3 asserts 'Because most audited pages share the same template, the pattern is likely present across the audited set' — the bare-div issue is evidenced on only one named page (https://typo3.org/association) yet the finding is extended with stated confidence to the full audited set of 7 pages without data from those other pages.
findings.context: Because most audited pages share the same template, the pattern is likely present across the audited set, though the figures cited are specific to https://typo3.org/association
